name: How to Minimize Change Orders on Los Angeles County Commercial Builds

mainEntity.name: What practical steps can Los Angeles County commercial owners take to reduce change orders during construction without driving up design costs?
mainEntity.text: What practical steps can Los Angeles County commercial owners take to reduce change orders during construction without driving up design costs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Change orders are a major source of budget and schedule risk in commercial construction, particularly in complex jurisdictions like Los Angeles County. Owners can reduce them without massively increasing design costs by focusing on a few high-impact practices. First, invest in a solid schematic design that resolves key program, structural, and systems decisions before rushing to permit. This allows the design team to coordinate plans across disciplines and catch conflicts early. Second, request a structured constructability review from the contractor during preconstruction. This should focus on access, sequencing, structural details, and building systems’ routing rather than only on unit pricing. Identifying hard-to-build details and revising them before bid reduces field changes. Third, use realistic allowances for finishes and equipment where selections are not finalized at bid time, and set clear processes and deadlines for owner decisions. Late selections and scope clarifications are a common source of change orders. Finally, maintain clear communication channels among the owner, architect, contractor, and key consultants. Rapid responses to requests for information (RFIs) and proactive resolution of issues prevent minor questions from turning into expensive redesigns. The modest additional effort and fees for targeted preconstruction coordination typically pay for themselves through fewer and smaller change orders.
acceptedAnswer.description: Reducing change orders in Los Angeles County commercial projects depends on thorough preconstruction planning, careful drawing coordination, conservative allowances for unknowns, and rapid decision-making by owners. Investing in targeted early design and constructability reviews often saves more in change orders than it costs in professional fees.
